content.value_statement: Developers lose time recreating small code patterns across projects. This skill helps save, tag, search, and improve reusable snippets for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
actual_capabilities: Defines a structured snippet format with language, category, tags, framework, use case, parameters, notes, and related snippets.
Provides example snippets for JavaScript, TypeScript, React, Python, Node.js, and SQL patterns.
Guides users to organize snippets by category, collection, framework, library, and reusable use case.
Documents file-based storage layouts and frontmatter metadata for snippet libraries.
Suggests maintenance practices for reviewing, testing, versioning, and cleaning up snippets.
limitations: Does not include an executable snippet database, web app, or command-line implementation.
Cannot persist snippets unless the host agent writes files or uses an external store.
Example snippets need review before production use.
Search quality depends on saved metadata, naming consistency, and prompt context.

use_cases.title: Build a personal snippet library
use_cases.description: Save repeated patterns with tags, descriptions, usage notes, and related examples for faster reuse.

use_cases.title: Standardize team code patterns
use_cases.description: Organize shared snippets by framework, category, and dependency so teams reuse approved implementation patterns.

use_cases.title: Improve coding documentation
use_cases.description: Add metadata, edge cases, parameters, and alternatives to snippets used in internal developer guides.

prompt_templates.title: Save a basic snippet
prompt_templates.prompt: Use snippet-manager to save this snippet. Add a short description, language, category, tags, parameters, and usage notes.

prompt_templates.title: Find related snippets
prompt_templates.prompt: Use snippet-manager to search for snippets about [topic]. Filter by [language] and suggest the best matches with reasons.

prompt_templates.title: Create a collection
prompt_templates.prompt: Use snippet-manager to organize my [project area] snippets into categories, tags, and a file-based folder plan.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a snippet library
prompt_templates.prompt: Use snippet-manager to review this snippet set for duplicates, missing metadata, outdated dependencies, edge cases, and replacement recommendations.

output_examples.input: Save a React debounce hook with usage guidance.
output: Creates a snippet entry with React, hooks, debounce, and performance tags.
Adds a concise use case, parameter notes, and related search terms.
Suggests testing behavior for changing values and cleanup timing.

output_examples.input: Find Python retry snippets for API calls.
output: Returns matching retry and backoff patterns with language and error-handling tags.
Highlights options for retry count, delay, backoff factor, and handled exceptions.
Notes that network examples require production review before use.
Groups query snippets into migrations, pagination, upsert, and reporting categories.
Recommends frontmatter fields for database engine, version, safety notes, and dependencies.

best_practices: Use clear names, stable categories, and multiple precise tags for every snippet.
Include dependencies, parameters, edge cases, and tested usage notes before sharing snippets.
Review snippets regularly for outdated APIs, insecure patterns, and duplicate implementations.
anti_patterns: Saving large files as snippets without a focused reuse purpose.
Keeping snippets without language, dependency, or version metadata.
Copying example snippets into production without testing and security review.

faq.question: Does this skill execute saved snippets?
faq.answer: No. It provides organization and documentation guidance for snippets, not an execution runtime.

faq.question: Can it create a persistent snippet database?
faq.answer: It can design a file layout and metadata format, but persistence depends on the host environment.

faq.question: Which languages are covered by the examples?
faq.answer: The document includes examples for JavaScript, TypeScript, React, Python, Node.js, and SQL.

faq.question: Can teams use it for shared standards?
faq.answer: Yes. Teams can use categories, tags, collections, and frontmatter metadata to standardize reusable patterns.

faq.question: Does it replace code review?
faq.answer: No. Snippets should still be tested and reviewed before use in production systems.

faq.question: How does search work?
faq.answer: The skill guides searches by language, category, tags, keywords, framework, library, and related patterns.
